title: Foreplay Homepage Teardown: Jan 2021 to Jan 2026
h1: How Foreplay rewrote its homepage over 5 years
metaTitle: Foreplay Homepage CRO Teardown — Jan 2021 to Jan 2026
description: A CRO teardown of Foreplay's homepage from Jan 2021 to Jan 2026 — what changed in headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation, and what SaaS teams can study from it.
excerpt: Foreplay's homepage didn't just get updated. The headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation all shifted in a consistent direction between Jan 2021 and Jan 2026. This teardown maps what changed, when, and what the patterns may suggest.
author: Wael Aouididi
authorBio: SaaS Growth Marketer and fractional growth lead. I help B2B SaaS founders diagnose landing page, CRO, positioning, and analytics leaks before scaling traffic.

lessonCards.title: Your H1 signals which buyer you are targeting
lessonCards.body: The headline changed from "We practice dope design & Sell Sh*t Online" to "The Complete Winning Ad Workflow". The framing of your H1 is one of the clearest signals of which buyer you are targeting and what you expect them to do next.

lessonCards.title: Navigation is a positioning statement
lessonCards.body: Navigation items changed from "Work", "Services", "Play Haus" to "Product", "API Leverage Foreplay data.", "Solutions". The labels your navigation uses reveal what you think your visitor is trying to decide — and who that visitor is.

lessonCards.title: Section headings reveal what the team thinks buyers care about
lessonCards.body: 8 section headings were added and 0 removed between Jan 2021 and Jan 2026. New headings include "Your new secret weapon for ads" and "Spark creative genius and crush competitors.". The pattern of what gets added and removed is one of the clearest signals of how a team is re-prioritizing its value proposition.

lessonCards.title: Incremental changes compound into a brand shift
lessonCards.body: Across 9 snapshots spanning roughly 5 years, no single update here was a dramatic overhaul. The end state looks very different from the start because small, consistent changes in the same direction accumulate. This is worth studying if your own homepage has been drifting without a clear direction.
